title: Security Posture Discovery - ACME Corp
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Initial security posture discovery focusing on ACME's compliance requirements (SOC2/ISO), identity integration (SAML/SSO), RBAC expectations, audit logging and retention, and encryption/KMS needs. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options and next steps to share SOC2 report, architecture diagram, and schedule a deeper security review.
next_steps: Laura to send current SOC 2 report and ISO 27001 cert link (by 2025-02-03)
Diego to share network architecture diagram for Redwood Private and VPC peering options (by 2025-02-05)
Schedule technical security review with ACME infra and security teams (propose slots next week)
Provide RBAC and SSO implementation notes and SAML metadata sample
action_items: Laura Chen: Send SOC2 report + ISO cert link - due 2025-02-03
Diego Patel: Share Redwood Private architecture diagram and VPC peering options - due 2025-02-05
Maya Rivers: Share ACME's required data retention policy and retention windows - due 2025-02-07
Tom Bryant: Confirm pilot scope and anticipated throughput for benchmarking - due 2025-02-04
transcript:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Laura from Redwood, with Diego, our solutions engineer. we really appreciate you taking time. quick intros?
[00:10] Maya (CISO - ACME): Hey, I'm Maya, CISO at ACME. we've been evaluating a few inference vendors, want to make sure security is rock solid before we proceed.
[00:18] Tom (CTO): Tom here, i'll be focused on architecture and perf.
[00:22] Lina (Infra): Lina, infra eng, i'll handle networking and deployment questions.
[00:26] Diego (Redwood SE): Hi all, Diego here. i'll jump into the technical bits and diagrams as needed.
[00:30] Laura: Great. high level agenda: compliance posture (SOC2/ISO), identity and auth (SSO/SAML, RBAC), audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS, and then deployment options - hosted vs dedicated vs private. any additions?
[00:42] Maya: sounds good. our big must-haves: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 is preferred, SSO via SAML with SCIM for provisioning, auditability, and customer-managed keys ideally. we also have strict data retention rules for PII.
[00:56] Diego: totally understood. quick note: Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem options. the private option supports customer-managed KMS and can be air-gapped.
[01:08] Tom: what's the difference between Dedicated and Private for us? cost aside, we need to know what we control versus Redwood controlling.
[01:15] Laura: good question. Dedicated is isolated by GPU pool and tenancy — you get capacity isolation and contractual data handling guarantees, but the control plane remains with Redwood. Private gives you a customer-controlled network boundary (VPC or on-prem) and optional private control plane for stricter compliance.
[01:30] Maya: so with Dedicated we can't bring our own KMS?
[01:33] Diego: correct, in Dedicated the KMS is Redwood-managed, but keys are rotated and encrypted at rest. for customer-managed keys you need Private, where we integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS or external HSM).
[01:45] Lina: network wise — does Redwood require inbound rules into our VPC for Private, or is it outbound-only peering?
[01:51] Diego: typically we do VPC peering or PrivateLink, it's configurable. for air-gapped on-prem we can do an installer package. we'll send the diagram but generally it's controlled, and we can avoid inbound internet exposure.
[02:05] Maya: about certifications, do you have SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001? can you share evidence?
[02:11] Laura: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. i'll share the redacted reports after an NDA or via the secure link.
[02:18] Tom: audit logs — what do they include? are token-level logs available? we'd like request-level tracing and retention for 1 year.
[02:25] Diego: we capture request metadata, timestamps, model version, latency, and error traces. payloads aren't stored by default in hosted for PII-sensitive customers; we also offer redaction and an option for longer retention as an enterprise add-on. token-level cost breakdown is available in the console.
[02:43] Maya: retention policy: our legal team requires 12 months of immutable audit logs with export capability. can we export logs to our S3/ELK?
[02:51] Laura: yes, for Dedicated and Private we can stream audit logs to your S3 or a SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). for hosted we have export options but there are contract and egress considerations.
[03:04] Lina: encryption at rest — what's the default? AES-256? and for in-transit TLS versions?
[03:10] Diego: default at-rest encryption is AES-256, in-transit TLS 1.2/1.3 with mutual TLS available for Private. for customer-managed keys we support AWS KMS and some HSM integrations.
[03:23] Maya: key rotation policy? who has access to keys?
[03:27] Diego: if Redwood-managed: we rotate keys per industry best practice quarterly and access is limited to our controls and audited. with customer-managed KMS, you control rotation and access. we don't have plaintext access to customer keys.
[03:41] Tom: what about RBAC — we need least-privilege admin roles, separation of duties, and SSO via SAML for SSO provisioning. can we map to our internal groups?
[03:50] Laura: yes, our console supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with admin, dev, read-only, and custom roles. mappings to your groups are supported; Diego can share mapping examples.
[04:03] Diego: quick note — some customers use SCIM for automated provisioning; others have manual invites. we also support MFA enforcement via SAML and conditional access policies if your identity provider supports it.
[04:16] Maya: any penetration testing or vulnerability disclosure programs? we need to know frequency and if third-party pen tests are available.
[04:22] Laura: we run quarterly internal vulnerability scans and annual third-party pen tests; results are available to customers under NDA. we also have a public security contact and bug bounty program details we can share.
[04:35] Lina: regarding data handling: for hosted, you mentioned payloads not stored by default for PII customers. is that opt-in or opt-out?
[04:42] Diego: it's opt-out by default for general hosted customers, but for enterprise customers we can configure no-persist modes or set up dedicated endpoints where logs are not retained. we'll capture telemetry needed for stability but can redact or avoid storing user content per contract.
[04:59] Maya: do you support data residency? e.g., store data in EU region only for our EU customers?
[05:04] Laura: yes, we have region controls and can enforce EU-only processing for data residency. Private deployment gives the highest assurance since you control region and network.
[05:14] Tom: for a pilot — we plan to test latency and throughput with about 200 concurrent sessions, average sequence lengths around 256 tokens. what's the audit around model variants and rollbacks? we need change control.
[05:25] Diego: we provide rollout controls: canary, A/B, rollbacks, and model pinning. all changes are logged, and you can require approval workflows in the console. we'll capture model version history in audit logs.
[05:37] Maya: how are third-party libraries and dependencies managed? supply chain concerns are high for us.
[05:42] Laura: we maintain SBOMs for our components and can provide them under NDA. we also have dependency scanning in our CI and a disclosure process for any critical CVEs.
[05:53] Lina: networking: will we need to open any inbound ports or will everything be outbound over peering?
[05:58] Diego: with VPC peering it's generally outbound from our side into your peered network, but specifics depend on the topology. we'll include both PrivateLink and peering options in the diagram.
[06:10] Tom: possibility of on-prem air-gapped? we have one environment that cannot reach internet for regulated workloads.
[06:16] Diego: yes, that's the air-gapped variant of Redwood Private. it requires an on-prem installer and we do offline key exchange; it's a bit more involved but supported.
[06:27] Maya: incident response — what's your SLA for security incidents and communication protocol?
[06:31] Laura: we have an incident response playbook; for high severity incidents we notify customers within one hour and provide a post-incident report. customers on enterprise support get a designated security liaison.
[06:43] Tom: do you offer contract clauses for data breaches and liability limits?
[06:46] Laura: yes, enterprise agreements include indemnity and specific security covenants; we'll have legal coordinate once you indicate interest.
[06:53] Maya: curious about auditability again — you mentioned immutable audit log option. is immutability provided via WORM storage or object locking?
[06:59] Diego: we support S3 Object Lock for WORM and can wire logs to an immutable storage account in your cloud. for some customers we also support push to third-party SIEM for immutable retention.
[07:12] Lina: what about data deletion when contract ends? do you provide certificate of deletion?
[07:16] Laura: yes, we provide data deletion process with a certificate of destruction/erasure, and we're able to purge keys and backups.
[07:24] Maya: ok, this is helpful. from a gating perspective we need to review SOC2, ISO docs, KMS integration details, and network architecture. after that, we may run a short POC in a Private or Dedicated environment.
[07:36] Tom: timeline wise — we're aiming to decide by end of February. want to kick off pilot early March if everything checks out.
[07:44] Laura: great — we'll turn around the docs quickly. Diego, can you take point on the diagrams and RBAC mapping examples?
[07:50] Diego: yep, i'll send a diagram and a sample SAML/SCIM metadata and RBAC mapping.
[07:55] Laura: i'll share the SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts via secure link, and coordinate legal touchpoint for an NDA if needed.
[08:02] Maya: thanks. one last thing — encryption in transit with mutual TLS, is that enforced for Private only or can it be used for Dedicated?
[08:08] Diego: mutual TLS is available for Private by default; Dedicated can be configured with mutual TLS for specific enterprise contracts. we'll note that in the follow-up.
[08:18] Laura: ok let's recap next steps and action items...
[08:22] [recap omitted for brevity]
[08:28] Laura: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed slots for the technical security review.
[08:34] Maya: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:36] Tom: thanks all.
[08:38] Lina: bye.
